name: PERCENTILE.INC
description: PERCENTILE.INC returns the k-th percentile of values using the inclusive method, where k is any number from 0 to 1 inclusive.
tldr: Returns the value at percentile k (0 <= k <= 1) using the inclusive method.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array of numeric values.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: The percentile, a number between 0 and 1 inclusive.

advancedExamples.title: 90th percentile with interpolation
advancedExamples.description: A high k produces a rank near the top of the list.

advancedExamples.title: k = 0 returns the minimum
advancedExamples.description: The inclusive method allows k = 0 and k = 1 at the extremes.
advancedExamples.explanation: With k = 0 the function returns the smallest value, 1.

howItWorks: PERCENTILE.INC uses the inclusive (INC) method. It computes a rank as 1 + k*(n-1), where n is the number of values, then linearly interpolates between the two surrounding sorted values. Because the method is inclusive, k can be 0 (minimum) or 1 (maximum). It is functionally identical to the legacy PERCENTILE. Text and logical values are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the percentile.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The interpolated percentile value is returned.

limitations: k must be between 0 and 1 inclusive, else #NUM!.
Interpolates between values, so the result may not be a real data point.

commonErrors.cause: k is outside 0..1 or the array is empty.
commonErrors.fix: Keep k between 0 and 1 and supply a non-empty numeric range.

commonErrors.cause: The two functions use different interpolation formulas.
commonErrors.fix: Use PERCENTILE.EXC only when you need the exclusive method (k strictly between 0 and 1).

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports PERCENTILE.INC with the same inclusive behavior as Excel 2010+.

faq.question: What is the difference between .INC and .EXC?
faq.answer: .INC (inclusive) allows k from 0 to 1 and uses rank 1 + k*(n-1); .EXC (exclusive) requires k strictly between 0 and 1 and uses rank k*(n+1), so it never returns the actual min or max.

faq.question: Is PERCENTILE.INC the same as PERCENTILE?
faq.answer: Yes. PERCENTILE is the legacy name for the inclusive method; PERCENTILE.INC is the Excel 2010+ equivalent.

faq.question: Why is my percentile a decimal?
faq.answer: The inclusive method interpolates between the two nearest values when the rank is fractional.
